Alex — thanks, that helps. We put together three distinct reserve choices that map to different activation runways and budget profiles. Attaching a compact PDF and the cost model. High level:

1) Stabilized Minimum (conservative spend)
   - Committed baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (min guaranteed, pooled)
   - Activation runway: full production throughput in ~2 weeks (warmup + KV priming)
   - Burst handling: short bursts via auto-burst pool (up to +30% sustained for 10m)
   - Ideal when you need SLA-backed latency and predictable billing

2) Staged Ramp (recommended for predictable growth)
   - Phase 1 (0-30 days): 8 GPUs baseline + 4 warm standby (reserved but sleepable)
   - Phase 2 (31-90 days): scale to 16 GPUs as traffic matures (can be pre-warmed)
   - Activation runway: initial lane within 48 hours, full ramp over 6–8 weeks
   - Includes warmup credits (1 week) and KV cache priming assistance

3) Elastic Buffer (cost-flex, quicker on-ramps)
   - Committed baseline: 4 GPUs + shared burst credits and priority lane slots
   - Burst pool: large burstable capacity with preemption policy and graceful fallback to 8-bit quantized model variants
   - Activation runway: minutes for small lanes, 72 hours for sustained lanes

I also included an appendix with SLA implications and a simple ramp table you can paste into the MOU. If procurement wants, we can convert the Staged Ramp to a two-tranche financial commit.

I've cc'd Ben and Rishi to help with the activation timeline and technical notes. Next step: sync with Procurement and pick which reserve choice maps to your acceptance criteria for latency and cost.

Vanessa

Attachments: reserve_options_NEMORA_v2.pdf, nemora_cost_model_v2.xlsx

Looping in some technical clarifications for the Staged Ramp plan. Highlights:

- Baseline sizing rationale: 8 GPUs maps to ~3.5k token/s sustained using the selected 16B model with quantization and batching. That covers your steady-state plus a safety margin.
- Warm standby mechanics: the 4 warm GPUs in phase 1 will be reserved capacity with reduced power state to minimize burn; they can be fully activated in ~4 hours and pre-warmed to reduce cold-start latency.
- Burst pool and failover: we recommend a fallback lane running a lightly quantized variant (Q4) that preserves quality for classification tasks during extreme bursts. Failover is automatic with transparent KPIs logged in the Console.
- KV priming: we’ll run a one-time priming job using the first 48 hours of production queries to seed the prefix cache — this reduces token cost by ~8–12% on typical chat flows.

I'll add a short activation checklist to the draft MOU (networking, allowlist IPs, KMS handoff, playbook for scaled activations).

Ben

Alex — thanks, happy to get this across the finish line. Per your asks we've attached a short MOU snippet (in the PDF) and added a "Fast Ramp" variant inside the Staged Ramp that shortens full activation to 4 weeks in exchange for a month-1 uplift in committed GPUs. Key points:

Fast Ramp (opt-in):
- Month 1 commit: 16 GPUs (pre-warmed pool), Month 2: 16 GPUs, Month 3: 12 GPUs (step-down), thereafter as per consumption or standard Step-Down schedule
- Activation: production throughput achievable within 7 days, full target SLA band within 28 days with aggressive pre-warm and KV priming jobs
- Uplift: ~22% higher month-1 cost vs standard Staged Ramp, includes 2 weeks of warmup credits and dedicated onboarding support

SLA note: the Elastic Buffer approach can meet 99th < 350ms for interactive chat only if you accept prioritized lanes for interactive traffic (we can reserve two low-latency lanes inside the burst pool). If you don't reserve those lanes, 99th will vary during sustained extreme bursts. The Staged Ramp/Fast Ramp guarantee the SLA with capacity-backed commitments.

Attached: reserve_options_NEMORA_v2.pdf (includes MOU snippets) and the requested single-line cost table. If Procurement gives green light on the Fast Ramp numbers, we can issue a redlined MOU within 24 hours and schedule the kickoff with our Onboarding team.

Thanks — looping Marissa to coordinate MOU revisions and Rishi to confirm final pricing and sales credits.
